scenes.title: Clinical wrap-up: the cell that reports "base" wherever it is
scenes.contentHtml:
Clinical wrap-up: the cell that reports "base" wherever it is

Here is a question the lesson's own machinery can answer, and it is a question about a disease.

Among colorectal cancers, about 93 per cent carry an activating mutation in the Wnt pathway, and the gene most often hit is APC. APC is the largest scaffolding component of the destruction complex, and it has appeared twice in this lesson already. Why should damaging a scaffold in a pathway that reports position produce a tumour?

Work the pathway instead of reaching for a general statement about cancer genes.

Following the lesion through the chain

APC has two jobs in what this lesson covered, and losing it interferes with both.

It is part of the destruction complex, the assembly that phosphorylates beta-catenin so that it is tagged and destroyed. And the colonocyte work in scene 2 found that full-length APC is required for the complex to reorient towards a Wnt cue. This is where the borrowed idea of separable protein parts earns its place: a shortened APC is still a protein and still does some of what APC does, and it has specifically lost the part needed for that reorientation.

The numbers from that study come with a condition attached. Three components of the complex were scored separately for whether they gathered towards Wnt-coated beads, and the figure depends on which one you follow: across Axin1, GSK3B and beta-catenin the proportion of cells showing the movement ran from 61 to 80 per cent when APC was full length. In a line expressing a truncated APC it fell to about 30 per cent, and where APC had been deleted outright the Wnt-induced localisation was abolished. So the range is a spread across the components measured, not an uncertainty about one of them.

Now put a cell with damaged APC anywhere you like in the crypt and trace scene 2 forward. The destruction complex is impaired, so beta-catenin is no longer cleared efficiently. Free beta-catenin accumulates. It reaches the nucleus, partners TCF and LEF, and switches on c-MYC, LGR5 and cyclin D1: the programme of a dividing, undifferentiated cell. All of that happens whether or not any Wnt arrived.

That last clause is the whole point, and it is a specific kind of failure. The gradient outside the cell is unchanged. The mesenchyme near the base is still secreting, the concentration still falls with height, the positional information is still sitting there in the fluid. What has broken is the reading. The output has become independent of the input, so the cell now reports "I am at the crypt base" at every height, and behaves accordingly at every height.

The same holds under either account of what the cell reads. If the readout tracks the absolute level, the level is now high everywhere. If instead it compares against a recent baseline, as scene 6's fold-change hypothesis proposes, then a cell whose destruction machinery is broken has lost the falling baseline that comparison depended on. Neither version leaves the cell able to locate itself, so the conclusion here does not rest on settling that question.

Read that against the opening of this lesson. The problem was a cell with no map and no address, solved by reading a concentration. A cell with damaged APC has lost the solution while keeping the problem. It is not receiving a wrong answer about where it is; it has stopped asking.

Why this tissue

The crypt is a place where that failure has unusual consequences, and two facts from earlier lessons in this block say why.

The colonic epithelium renews itself on a timescale of a few days, with absorptive cells replaced every four to five days. And the architecture of the crypt, the stem cells at the base and the differentiation that proceeds as cells climb, is organised by the gradient this lesson has been describing. A tissue that rebuilds itself that fast is a tissue in which the instruction "divide and stay undifferentiated" is being issued and withdrawn continuously, in the right places, over and over for a lifetime in every crypt. Removing the withdrawal step from that arrangement is a serious matter in a way it would not be in a tissue that renews once a decade.

How that becomes a tumour, what else has to go wrong, how the process is staged and detected: none of that is this lesson's material. Lesson 08 of this block (PREM-05.08) takes up the cell cycle that the stem-cell programme is driving, and lesson 10 of this block (PREM-05.10) takes up cell death, senescence and cancer, where this thread is picked up properly. What this lesson hands them is the reading mechanism and a precise account of the joint that fails.

Callout
id callout-clinical-boundary

A teaching example, not medical advice. This scene traces a published molecular account and nothing more. No patient, drug, dose or recommendation appears in it, and nothing here supports a diagnosis, prognosis, screening or treatment decision. The 93 per cent is a population figure from a review; it is not anyone's personal risk.

What the lesson established

A cell in a tube 32 cells tall works out where it is by measuring how much of one substance reaches it, and that measurement runs through four parts and a fifth job: a signal, a receptor, transduction, a response, and the capacity to stop.

The measurement is bounded, and the bounds are countable. One threshold on one falling gradient separates two regions and no more, and nested thresholds add zones far faster than they add bits. Precision is bought with averaging time, at four times the time for half the uncertainty, spent by a cell that is moving while it counts.

On amplification the honest result is narrower than the textbook slogan. The identifiable catalytic steps in the canonical Wnt pathway sit on the arm that destroys the output rather than the arm that produces it, and the output shifts about sixfold between two resting levels. Phototransduction, measured a different way, hydrolyses more than 100,000 molecules per absorbed photon. Those two figures cannot be divided into one another, and the lesson traced per-step amplification through phototransduction and a constructed example because the per-step figures for Wnt were not available.

How the gradient is built is partly unsettled, and so is how Wnt binding slows the destruction. The lesson said which of its own statements would survive either answer.

And the reading can fail in a way that leaves the gradient intact. That is where this block goes next.

assessment.title: Reading a position from a concentration: pathway, bounds, and confidence

items.prompt: Put the six events of canonical Wnt signalling in a colonic crypt cell into the order in which they are observed, starting with the earliest. Order them by when each is seen, not by which one you think causes the next: this lesson records that how membrane recruitment leads to the rise in beta-catenin is unsettled.

options.text: The amount of available free beta-catenin rises.
c-MYC, LGR5 and cyclin D1 are switched on.
Mesenchymal cells near the crypt base secrete Wnt ligands.
The destruction complex is recruited to the cell membrane.
Beta-catenin reaches the nucleus and acts with TCF and LEF.
Wnt binds the receptor complex of Frizzled with LRP5/6.

answer.summary: Secretion, receptor binding, recruitment of the destruction complex, the rise in free beta-catenin, the nuclear partnership with TCF and LEF, then transcription. This is the observed sequence; the step from recruitment to the rise is not a settled mechanism.
answer.reasoning:
The chain runs from outside the cell inward. Mesenchymal cells near the base are the source, so secretion comes first. Wnt then binds Frizzled with LRP5/6, which is the reception step. Binding leads to the destruction complex being recruited to the membrane. Because that complex is what marks beta-catenin for proteasomal degradation, interfering with it lets free beta-catenin rise; the rise follows the recruitment rather than causing it, which is the ordering learners most often invert. Beta-catenin then reaches the nucleus and acts with TCF and LEF, and that partnership switches on c-MYC, LGR5 and cyclin D1.

One caution for the marker, and it is the reason this item asks for an observed sequence. Recruitment of the destruction complex to the membrane is seen before free beta-catenin rises, and that ordering is what the item tests. It is not a claim that recruitment is the sufficient cause of the rise. This pack records that relocation is partial and does not by itself account for the loss of destruction activity, with saturation by already-phosphorylated beta-catenin and impaired ubiquitin ligase docking also under consideration. A learner who orders these correctly and adds that the causal link is unsettled has given the better answer, and must not be marked down for it.
acceptableResponses: Secretion by mesenchyme, Wnt binds Frizzled and LRP5/6, destruction complex recruited to the membrane, free beta-catenin rises, beta-catenin acts with TCF and LEF, target genes switched on.
commonErrors: Placing the rise in beta-catenin before the recruitment of the destruction complex, which reverses cause and effect: the complex has to be interfered with before beta-catenin can accumulate.
Placing the TCF and LEF partnership before the rise in beta-catenin, which skips the step that makes enough beta-catenin available to reach the nucleus.
Treating Wnt binding as switching on beta-catenin production rather than blocking its destruction; the order is the same but the stated reason is wrong, and the misconception shows up in later items.

items.prompt: A quantitative model of the canonical Wnt pathway reports these four figures. Axin is present at about 20 picomolar and APC at about 100 nanomolar. Doubling Axin shortens beta-catenin's half-life by about 50 per cent; doubling GSK3B shortens it by about 10 per cent. Which explanation of that difference in sensitivity do the figures support?

options.text: Axin is by far the scarcest of the major components, about 5000-fold less abundant than APC, so it is what limits how much destruction complex can be assembled; adding to the component in shortest supply changes throughput most.
GSK3B should have been the more sensitive one because it is the kinase that attaches the phosphate, and the 10 per cent figure must therefore reflect measurement error in the model.
APC at 100 nanomolar is the most abundant component, so it contributes most of the complex's activity and Axin's effect must come from stabilising APC.
The components act as one complex, so the difference between 50 and 10 per cent cannot be explained by their concentrations and must come from the order in which they bind.

answer.summary: Axin is the scarce, limiting component: about 5000-fold less abundant than APC, so adding to it changes throughput most.
answer.reasoning: Put the two concentrations in one unit before comparing them, which the stem invites: 100 nanomolar is 100,000 picomolar, so APC is present at roughly 5000 times Axin's concentration. A component that scarce is the one that runs out, and therefore the one that limits how much working destruction complex can exist. Doubling it increases the amount of complex and speeds beta-catenin's clearance, which is the 50 per cent figure. Doubling a component already in large excess changes little, because it was never the shortage. The GSK3B option confuses being essential with being rate-limiting: GSK3B does the chemistry and the pathway cannot work without it, but that is a different property from controlling the rate, and only the second is what a doubling tests. Nothing in the figures supports treating the 10 per cent as error, and nothing supports Axin acting through APC.
acceptableResponses: Axin, because at about 20 picomolar against 100 nanomolar it is roughly 5000-fold scarcer and therefore the limiting component.
Axin is the component in shortest supply, so it caps how much complex can form; GSK3B is essential but not rate-limiting.
commonErrors: Choosing GSK3B on the reasoning that the enzyme doing the chemistry must be rate-limiting. The chemistry is right and the inference is not.
Failing to convert units, and so treating 20 picomolar and 100 nanomolar as comparable numbers.
Choosing APC by equating abundance with influence. Its abundance is exactly why it is not the sensitive point.

items.prompt: A crypt of the descending colon is about 32 cells along its length. Suppose, for the sake of the calculation, that every one of those 32 positions had to be told apart from every other. How many binary yes-or-no distinctions would that require? Give a whole number.

answer.summary: 5 bits, because 32 halves to 1 in five steps.
answer.reasoning: Each yes-or-no question can at best halve the number of remaining candidates. Starting from 32: sixteen, eight, four, two, one. That is five questions, and five binary distinctions is five bits. Equivalently the base-2 logarithm of 32 is 5. Note what the number is and is not. It is the demand that would be created by the supposition in the question. It is not a measurement of the crypt and not a claim that the crypt encodes five bits; the lesson's argument is that the supposition is the part to reject, because a crypt has no use for 32 separate addresses.
acceptableResponses: five
log base 2 of 32, which is 5
commonErrors: Answering 32, which restates the number of positions rather than the number of distinctions needed to separate them.
Answering 31, which is the number of thresholds needed to cut an axis into 32 zones, a different quantity asked about elsewhere in the lesson.
Answering 16, which is one halving rather than the count of halvings.
Answering 6, from rounding up a logarithm that is already a whole number; 2 to the power 5 is exactly 32, so no rounding is needed.

items.prompt: A tissue reads one substance whose concentration falls monotonically along an axis. It reads that gradient using genes which act independently of one another and which each switch at a single threshold. How many such thresholds are needed to divide the axis into 8 distinguishable zones? Give a whole number.

answer.summary: 7 thresholds, because k cuts along a line produce k plus 1 pieces.
answer.reasoning: On a concentration that falls in one direction, each threshold marks one place along the axis where a gene changes state. Those places are cuts in a line, and k cuts divide a line into k plus 1 segments. For 8 segments, k plus 1 equals 8, so k equals 7. Every stipulation the answer needs is in the question: the gradient is monotonic, so each threshold is crossed once; the genes are independent and single-threshold, so no gene supplies more than one boundary. This is why reading a single gradient with independent thresholds is an expensive way to encode position, and it is the calculation that motivates looking for something better.
acceptableResponses: seven
k + 1 = 8 so k = 7
commonErrors: Answering 8, by matching one threshold to each zone. Count the boundaries between zones instead: eight zones have seven internal boundaries.
Answering 3, which is the number of bits needed to label 8 positions. Bits and thresholds are different quantities, and this question asks for thresholds.
Answering 4, by halving the number of zones, which corresponds to no step in the argument.

items.prompt: In a quantitative model of the canonical Wnt pathway built on measurements in frog egg extracts, moving from the unstimulated reference state to the standard stimulated state raised free beta-catenin from about 25 nanomolar to about 153 nanomolar. Separately, a textbook reports that vertebrate phototransduction hydrolyses more than 100,000 cyclic GMP molecules for a single absorbed quantum of light. Which conclusion do these two figures together support?

options.text: Free beta-catenin rose about sixfold, a real but modest change; and because that figure is a ratio of two steady-state concentrations while the phototransduction figure counts molecules per input event, the two cannot be compared numerically at all.

Dividing 100,000 by 6 shows that phototransduction amplifies about seventeen thousand times more strongly than the Wnt pathway, so vision is the better-amplified cascade by roughly four orders of magnitude.
Both pathways amplify by more than 100,000-fold, because a multi-step signalling chain is a cascade and cascades multiply their input at every step.
A sixfold change is within measurement noise, so the Wnt figure shows that this pathway does not transmit its signal to beta-catenin at all.

answer.summary: About sixfold, and the two figures are different kinds of quantity, so no numerical comparison between the pathways is available.
answer.reasoning: Two separate judgements are needed and both must be right. First the arithmetic: 153 divided by 25 is about 6, so the change is real and modest. Second, and this is what the item is really testing, the two numbers do not measure the same kind of thing. The Wnt figure is a dimensionless ratio between two resting concentrations, with no time and no per-event count in it. The phototransduction figure is a tally of molecules hydrolysed per single absorbed photon, accumulated by enzymes turning over. Dividing one by the other produces a number with no meaning, so the tempting 'four orders of magnitude' conclusion is not supported by this evidence, however often it is repeated. What the pair does support is that the word cascade fixes neither the size of a gain nor even the units it is reported in. The other two options fail on the figures themselves: 100,000-fold contradicts the quoted Wnt values and reads amplification out of a label, and a sixfold rise is a clear change rather than noise.
acceptableResponses: About sixfold; and the two figures cannot be compared numerically because one is a steady-state ratio and the other a per-event catalytic count.
153 over 25 is roughly 6, a modest change, and comparing that with a per-photon molecule tally is a category error.
commonErrors: Dividing 100,000 by 6 to get a ratio of gains. This is the error the item is built around: the two quantities have different units and different meanings, so their quotient is not a gain ratio.
Assuming a multi-step pathway must have very high gain, which reads the amplification out of the word cascade instead of out of a measurement.
Treating a sixfold change as negligible. Small relative to another pathway is not the same as absent.
Concluding that the response is all-or-none. Two steady-state levels cannot show the shape of a dose-response relationship.

items.prompt: A revision guide states: "The Wnt gradient in the intestinal crypt is produced by the diffusion of Wnt away from source cells at the crypt base." In your own words, and in four short parts: (a) say what this sentence gets right; (b) say precisely what it asserts beyond what the evidence supports; (c) name one alternative account of Wnt spread reported in the literature, with the observation behind it; (d) name one statement from earlier in this lesson that would still stand if the diffusion account turned out to be wrong for the human colon, and say why it is unaffected.

answer.correct: (a) The source and the direction are right: mesenchymal cells near the crypt base secrete Wnt, cells further away do not, and Wnt activity falls progressively up the crypt axis. (b) The mechanism is the overstatement. Saying diffusion produces the profile asserts a settled mechanism where the literature describes the range of Wnt action as long debated and not known, and where Wnt proteins are hydrophobic because of a lipid modification, which is what makes travel through aqueous space hard to explain in the first place. (c) One alternative: short-range spread by lateral transcytosis, in which the ligand is handed between neighbouring cells rather than released to diffuse, reported for Wnt3 in mouse intestinal crypts. Others proposed include carriage on lipoproteins, on heparan sulphate proteoglycans, in exosomes, or along cytonemes; travel as oligomers or micelles was proposed and then argued against, because blocking the movement of one labelled form of Wingless in flies did not affect the spreading of a differently labelled form. (d) Any statement downstream of the ligand reaching a receptor. For example, that the destruction complex including APC, Axin, CK1A and GSK3B marks beta-catenin for degradation, and that Wnt binding to Frizzled with LRP5/6 raises available beta-catenin by interfering with that destruction. It is unaffected because it describes what happens once Wnt arrives at a receptor, which is downstream of however the Wnt got there.
answer.summary: Right about source and direction; overstated about mechanism; the short-range handover reading is a live alternative; everything downstream of receptor binding survives either way.
answer.reasoning: The item tests whether a learner can hold one sentence at two different confidence levels at once, which is the calibration skill the scene is built around. Part (a) requires separating the profile, which the sources state plainly, from its cause. Part (b) requires naming the specific overreach rather than rejecting the sentence wholesale; the sentence is not simply wrong, and a response that calls the whole thing false has misread the evidence in the other direction. Part (c) requires a named alternative with its evidence, not merely an assertion that alternatives exist. Part (d) tests the structural point that a mechanism dispute about delivery does not propagate downstream of delivery: the reception, transduction and response steps are indifferent to how the ligand arrived. A response naming any claim from the transduction or response scenes, with that reasoning, earns the marks.
acceptableResponses: Any response that identifies the source and falling direction as supported, identifies diffusion as the unsupported part, names lateral transcytosis or another reported route with its supporting observation, and names any post-receptor step as unaffected with the reason that it sits downstream of delivery.
A response that names the anti-oligomer Wingless labelling experiment as the observation in part (c) instead of the transcytosis result, provided the rest is intact.

A response that in part (d) names the one-bit ceiling on threshold reading, on the grounds that the information argument requires only that some graded quantity is being read and not any particular means of spreading.

A response that answers part (c) with the destruction-complex question instead of a transport route, naming saturation of the complex with already-phosphorylated beta-catenin or blocked docking of the ubiquitin-attaching enzyme as competing proposals, provided parts (a), (b) and (d) are intact.
commonErrors: Rejecting the whole sentence as false. The source and the direction of the gradient are well supported, and only the mechanism is overstated.
Answering part (b) with a general remark that biology is complicated, instead of naming diffusion as the specific claim that exceeds the evidence.
Naming an alternative in part (c) without the observation behind it, which repeats the original error of asserting a mechanism without evidence.
Claiming in part (d) that the whole pathway would have to be rewritten. The reception, transduction and response steps are downstream of delivery and do not depend on how the ligand travelled.

Choosing for part (d) a statement about the shape of the concentration profile or a calculation of gradient shape from a diffusion coefficient. Those are exactly the statements that would be affected, which is why the lesson does not make them.

items.prompt: A cell sits high in a crypt, where Wnt is low, and it carries a truncated APC that has lost the regions required for efficient beta-catenin degradation. Predict its level of free beta-catenin and whether its beta-catenin-dependent gene programme is running, giving the reason from the pathway. Then say in one sentence what that cell has lost about its ability to read its position. Finally, state one thing your prediction does not establish, and one feature of the truncation that would change it.

answer.correct:
Free beta-catenin is high and the gene programme is running, despite the low Wnt. The reason is that APC has two roles here: it is a component of the destruction complex that marks beta-catenin for proteasomal degradation, and full-length APC is required for that complex to reorient towards a Wnt cue. With APC truncated, beta-catenin is not cleared efficiently, so it accumulates, reaches the nucleus, acts with TCF and LEF, and switches on c-MYC, LGR5 and cyclin D1. What the cell has lost is the link between input and output: its beta-catenin level no longer tracks the Wnt concentration around it, so it reports the crypt base at any height rather than receiving a wrong answer about where it is. What the prediction does not establish: that this change by itself produces a tumour; anything about an individual person's risk, diagnosis, prognosis or treatment; or which specific truncation produces which degree of decoupling.

What the prediction does not establish: that the cell is fully independent of Wnt. The study this lesson cites reports that truncated APC retains some localisation towards a Wnt cue and discusses retained partial regulation, and this pack's own claim records that how far the readout is decoupled depends on which part of APC is lost. So the honest prediction is a cell whose beta-catenin level is high and largely uncoupled from its position, not one in which the pathway has been disconnected.

The feature that would change it: which regions the truncation removes, and what the other allele carries. A shorter truncation retaining more beta-catenin binding and degradation capacity leaves more regulation intact, and the degree of decoupling varies with the allelic combination. That is why the stem specifies the regions lost rather than saying only that APC is truncated.
answer.summary: Beta-catenin high and the programme on despite low Wnt, because damaged APC breaks the destruction step; the cell's output has been decoupled from its input, and the prediction establishes nothing clinical.
answer.reasoning:
This item runs the pathway from scene 2 forward under a single alteration, which is the transfer the lesson is built towards. The mechanism has two supported parts: APC belongs to the destruction complex whose loss of function permits beta-catenin accumulation, and the colonocyte study found reorientation of the complex towards a localised Wnt cue falling from 61 to 80 per cent of cells with full-length APC to about 30 per cent with truncated APC, and abolished where APC was deleted. Either route leaves beta-catenin uncleared. The positional sentence is the part that matters most: the gradient outside the cell is unchanged and the information is still present, so the failure is in the reading rather than in the signal. The final part is required because the lesson's own claim ledger records the positional interpretation as an inference and the mutation frequency as a population figure, and a learner who states a limit is doing what the lesson asks. A response that predicts high beta-catenin without naming the destruction step earns partial credit only, because the prediction without the mechanism does not show the pathway has been traced.

Do not award full marks for an answer that reports complete Wnt independence as a categorical consequence of any truncation. The stem now fixes which regions are lost precisely so the prediction is answerable; the final part asks the learner to notice that a different truncation gives a different answer. This is a health-sensitive item and the overgeneralisation is the error it exists to catch.
acceptableResponses: High beta-catenin and the programme on, because the truncated APC leaves the destruction complex unable to clear beta-catenin, so the output is now independent of the Wnt input and the cell behaves as though at the base; and the prediction says nothing about causing cancer in any individual or about diagnosis or treatment.
A response that names only the destruction complex membership role of APC, without the relocation result, provided the prediction and the decoupling statement are correct and a limit is stated.

A response whose stated limit is that other changes are needed for a tumour, or that cultured cell lines are not a crypt, or that the positional interpretation is the lesson's inference rather than a quoted finding.
commonErrors: Predicting low beta-catenin, by treating APC as something that promotes beta-catenin rather than as part of the machinery that destroys it.
Predicting that nothing happens because Wnt is low. This misses the point of the item: the lesion removes the cell's dependence on Wnt.
Describing the cell as receiving incorrect positional information. The gradient outside is unchanged and the information is intact; what has failed is the reading of it.

Stating or implying a diagnosis, a prognosis, a screening recommendation or a treatment. The item asks for a molecular prediction and an explicit limit, and any clinical recommendation is outside what the lesson supports.
Omitting the final part. A prediction offered without its limit is incomplete on this item's rubric.

items.prompt: A hormone is lipid-soluble and crosses the plasma membrane unaided. Its receptor is intracellular and belongs to the nuclear receptor superfamily. Which statement about that receptor is supported by this lesson's sources?

options.text: The transduction job does not arise for it, because there is no extracellular binding event to convert into an intracellular one, and it mediates transcription without intermediate signalling cascades by binding its target genes directly.
Because it binds its target genes directly, with no intermediate cascade, its response must appear faster than the response of a receptor tyrosine kinase.
It must still convert an extracellular binding event into an intracellular one through a second messenger, because every receptor performs transduction by definition.
Its architecture predicts a response on the millisecond to sub-millisecond timescale, the figure established for receptors whose ligand binding gates a channel directly.

answer.summary: No transduction step is needed, because the ligand crosses the membrane itself, and the source states that nuclear receptors mediate transcription without intermediate signalling cascades and bind target genes directly.
answer.reasoning:
Two sourced facts do the work. Nuclear receptors do not sit in the plasma membrane, and their ligands cross it, so there is no extracellular event that has to be turned into an intracellular one. And the feature the source names as distinguishing them from other kinds of receptor is that they mediate transcription without intermediate signalling cascades, binding target genes directly.

The attractive wrong answer is the speed one, and it is the error this item exists to catch. A shorter chain is a structural fact about how many stages lie between binding and transcription. Converting it into a claim about how long the response takes requires knowing how long each stage lasts, and transcription and translation are not instantaneous. No source in this pack measures the response time of a nuclear receptor or of a receptor tyrosine kinase, so no ranking between them can be asserted, in either direction. A learner who says the step count is smaller and stops there has the supported answer.

The millisecond option misapplies the one timescale figure this pack carries. That figure was established in chemosensory systems and describes receptors whose ligand binding gates an ion channel directly; it says nothing about intracellular receptors. The second-messenger option contradicts the definition of the class and would make transduction a step every receptor performs, which the nuclear receptor case shows it is not.
acceptableResponses: No transduction across the membrane is needed, because the ligand crosses on its own, and the receptor binds target genes directly without an intermediate cascade.
It skips the transduction job entirely; the source says nuclear receptors mediate transcription without intermediate signalling cascades.
commonErrors: Reading a shorter chain as a faster response. The number of stages and the duration of the response are different quantities, and this pack sources only the first.
Extending the millisecond to sub-millisecond figure beyond the direct-gating architecture and the chemosensory systems it was established in.
Assuming every receptor must transduce, which the intracellular receptor case is the counterexample to.

items.prompt: Frizzled's chain crosses the membrane seven times, and Frizzleds are assigned to class F of the G-protein-coupled receptors and were grouped in the IUPHAR GPCR database as the class FZD within the GPCR superfamily. From this a classmate concludes that Frizzled must therefore signal through a heterotrimeric G protein. Which response is best supported by the sources this lesson uses?

options.text: The classification is real and its grounds are on the record, but it does not settle the mechanism. Frizzleds show limited direct G-protein coupling and lack the DRY motif, one review calls the seven-transmembrane domain's contribution to signal transduction contentious and reports debate over classifying them strictly as GPCRs, while other authors call the supporting observation compelling and argue the controversy is smaller than it appears. The question is open.
The classification settles it. Membership of class F means the receptor couples to heterotrimeric G proteins, which is what the class is defined by.
The classification is an error that the literature has now corrected. Because Frizzleds lack the DRY motif, they are not G-protein-coupled receptors.
The question is settled in the negative, because canonical Wnt signalling is known to proceed without any involvement of heterotrimeric G proteins.

answer.summary: The class F assignment is real and documented, and whether Frizzleds should be classified strictly as GPCRs is disputed. The sources support reporting the dispute, not resolving it in either direction.
answer.reasoning:
The formal placement is sourced: the IUPHAR review records that Frizzleds were grouped separately as the class FZD within the GPCR superfamily, on the grounds of seven-transmembrane segments, evidence for coupling between Frizzleds and G proteins, and substantial structural differences from classes A, B and C.

The dispute is equally sourced, and it runs in both directions. A 2025 review states that the exact contributions of the seven-transmembrane domain to signal transduction are contentious and that, because Frizzleds show limited direct G-protein coupling, there is debate over whether they should be classified strictly as GPCRs. Against that, the IUPHAR review calls the basic observation supporting their nature as GPCRs compelling while saying the coupling remains to be fully explored, and a 2021 structural study argues that the apparent controversy is smaller than it first seems.

So the two failure modes are symmetrical and both are marked wrong here. Treating the classification as settling the mechanism ignores the debate and the missing DRY motif. Declaring that Frizzleds are not GPCRs overstates the other side: no source consulted says the classification has been corrected, and two of the three lean toward Frizzleds being genuine GPCRs. The fourth option asserts a settled negative that this pack has not established either; the pack's own Wnt trace simply does not invoke a heterotrimeric G protein, which is a statement about what that account needs and not a demonstration that no coupling occurs.

A learner who selects the correct option and adds that nothing else in this lesson depends on the answer has given the better response and should not be marked down.
acceptableResponses: The seven-pass architecture and the class F assignment are real, but they fix the family and not the mechanism; whether Frizzleds are strictly GPCRs is under debate and this lesson does not resolve it.

Both positions are held in the literature: limited direct G-protein coupling and no DRY motif on one side, a compelling basic observation and an argument that the controversy is overstated on the other.
commonErrors: Treating a structural classification as a demonstration of mechanism.
Flipping to the opposite certainty and declaring that Frizzleds are not GPCRs because they lack the DRY motif; no source consulted goes that far.
Citing this pack's Wnt trace as evidence that no G protein is involved. The trace does not need one, which is different from showing there is none.

items.prompt: Two cells sit side by side at the same height in a colonic crypt. One becomes an absorptive colonocyte and the other a secretory goblet cell. Answer four things. (a) Why can no threshold placed on the Wnt gradient account for the difference between them? (b) The crypt also carries a BMP gradient running the other way along the same axis. Explain why adding a BMP reading does not resolve part (a) either, and say what a second anti-parallel gradient can still plausibly offer. (c) Name the kind of input that can separate the two cells, and say what makes it different in kind from a gradient. (d) State one thing about how Wnt and Notch act together that the sources in this lesson do not settle.

answer.correct: Both cells sit at the same Wnt concentration, so any threshold on it returns the same value for both; BMP is a function of the same coordinate and so carries nearly the same information, though it can still give a second reading of that coordinate and place an opposing activity at the far end of the axis; a contact-dependent input such as Notch, whose ligands sit on neighbouring cells, reports adjacency instead of height and can therefore separate them; and the sources do not settle whether the Wnt and Notch relationship is synergistic or opposing.
answer.summary: Height cannot distinguish two cells at the same height, and neither can a second gradient on the same axis. A contact-dependent input reports something the axis does not. Whether Wnt and Notch cooperate or oppose is unresolved.
answer.reasoning:
Part (a) is the core of the item. The two cells are at one height, so they are at one Wnt concentration, and a threshold is a rule applied to that concentration. Applying the same rule to the same value returns the same answer, so no placement of any threshold, and no number of thresholds, separates them. This is the bound the earlier scene established, applied to a case where it bites.

Part (b) tests whether the learner has understood redundancy instead of memorising that more inputs are better. BMP runs along the same axis and falls the other way, so a BMP reading is close to a restatement of the Wnt reading: both are functions of the single coordinate of height, and two readings of one coordinate do not supply two coordinates. Credit an answer that also names what the second gradient can still offer: a second measurement of the same noisy quantity, and an active opponent at the far end of the axis so the difference between the ends is enforced from both directions. Do not require a number. This pack quantifies none of it, and states in the scene that the redundancy argument is its own reasoning applied to sourced facts.

Part (c) wants Notch, and wants the reason. Its ligands are membrane proteins carried on neighbouring cells, so the receptor is triggered on cell-to-cell contact. What it reports is which cells are adjacent, which is not a function of height, so it is not redundant with the axis in the way BMP is. Naming Notch without the contact-dependence earns partial credit only, because the mechanism is what makes the answer an explanation.

Part (d) has more than one acceptable answer and any genuine one counts: whether the relationship is synergistic or opposing; whether the interaction has a mechanism in the normal colon; or whether the mouse small-intestinal evidence transfers to the human colon. Do not accept an answer that states a direction as settled. One review says Wnt synergises with Notch to sustain undifferentiated proliferative stem and progenitor cells, and the same section reports Notch inhibition depleting stem cells while Wnt signalling rose, rescued by repressing Wnt, which its authors read as opposing and interconnected activities. Both trace to one primary study and the review reconciles neither.
acceptableResponses: (a) Same height means the same Wnt level, so any threshold on that level gives both cells the same answer. (b) BMP varies with the same coordinate in the opposite direction, so it largely restates the Wnt reading; it can still give a second noisy reading of height and an opposing activity at the top of the axis. (c) Notch, a contact-dependent input whose ligands sit on adjacent cells, so it reports neighbours instead of height. (d) Whether Wnt and Notch cooperate or oppose one another is not settled by these sources.

(a) A threshold applied to one concentration cannot separate two cells at that concentration. (b) A second gradient on the same axis is redundant with the first; what it adds is a repeat measurement and an opposing influence, not more addresses. (c) A cell-contact signal, Notch. (d) The sources give no mechanism for the Wnt and Notch interaction in the normal colon.
commonErrors: Answering that a steeper or better-placed Wnt threshold would separate the cells. The value being thresholded is identical for both, so no placement helps.
Treating the BMP gradient as an independent second axis and concluding that two gradients double the distinguishable positions.
Naming Notch without saying that its ligands are on neighbouring cells, which is the property that makes it different in kind from a gradient.
Stating that Wnt and Notch cooperate, or that they oppose, as though the sources settled it. Both readings are reported and neither is resolved.
