claims.scope: The chemical property of Wnt proteins that makes their spread difficult to explain, and the requirement for lipid modification in secretion.
claims.uncertainty: The review states the requirement for palmitoylation and the consequence of losing it. The lesson does not describe the chemistry of the modification, which belongs to lipid and protein chemistry outcomes elsewhere in the course.

claims.statement: Whether Wnts act as long-range signalling molecules has been a long-debated question and the exact range of their action is not known; lipoproteins, heparan sulphate proteoglycans, exosomes and cytonemes have each been proposed as transport routes, with some mechanisms operating simultaneously and others context-dependent, and the proposal that Wnts travel as oligomers or micelles is contradicted by the finding in flies that blocking the movement of one labelled form of Wingless did not affect the spreading of a differently labelled form.
claims.scope: The unsettled state of the mechanism by which Wnt ligands spread from their source, and the specific proposals under consideration.
claims.uncertainty: This claim records that the field is unsettled, which is what the review states; it is not a claim that any one mechanism is correct. The review's own hedging language includes remains unclear, poorly understood, controversial, and proposed mechanism, and the lesson carries the uncertainty at that level. Much of the underlying work is in Drosophila rather than human colon.

claims.statement: Analysis of Wnt3 in mouse intestinal crypts showed a short-range distribution mediated via lateral transcytosis, meaning the ligand is passed between neighbouring cells rather than released to diffuse freely through the extracellular space.
claims.scope: The reported mode of Wnt3 spread in mouse intestinal crypts, presented as one of the competing readings of how a crypt gradient is formed.
claims.uncertainty: The lesson reads this in a 2021 review that reports a 2016 primary study; the primary study was not itself retrieved, and the lesson attributes the finding to work reported in the review rather than presenting it as first-hand. The work is in mouse small intestine and concerns Wnt3, whereas this block follows the human colonic crypt, where the review identifies the mesenchyme rather than Paneth cells as the ligand source. The lesson therefore presents this as a reading to hold open rather than as the established mechanism for the human colon.

claims.statement: In the modelled canonical Wnt pathway, doubling the Axin concentration causes a 50 per cent drop in the half-life of beta-catenin, while doubling GSK3B decreases that half-life by about 10 per cent.
claims.scope: The relative sensitivity of beta-catenin half-life to the concentrations of two destruction complex components, in a fitted model of the pathway.
claims.uncertainty: These are model sensitivities computed for a frog egg extract system, not measurements in a human crypt cell, and a doubling is a modelling perturbation rather than an experiment performed on tissue. The lesson uses them to compare two components within one model and does not claim the percentages transfer to any other system.

claims.statement: Axin is present at about 20 picomolar, much lower than the concentration of the other major components of the Wnt pathway, against an APC concentration of about 100 nanomolar.
claims.scope: The concentrations of Axin and APC reported in a quantitative study of the pathway, used to explain why the system's sensitivity is concentrated in Axin.
claims.uncertainty: Measured in Xenopus egg extracts, so the absolute concentrations are properties of that system. The lesson's explanation, that adding to the scarcest component changes throughput more than adding to an abundant one, is a reading of the scarcity together with the sensitivity result rather than a separate sourced finding.

claims.statement: About 93 per cent of colorectal cancers contain an activating mutation in the Wnt pathway, particularly in APC, and loss of APC function impairs the destruction complex and allows beta-catenin to accumulate.
claims.scope: The frequency of Wnt pathway activating mutations among colorectal cancers, and the molecular consequence of losing APC function, used to motivate why a positional-signal pathway matters clinically.
claims.uncertainty: A population-level frequency quoted in a review, not a personal risk and not a statement about any individual. It depends on the cohorts and sequencing methods behind it and on how an activating mutation is defined. The lesson makes no claim about how such a mutation leads to a tumour, about staging, screening, prognosis or treatment, and defers cancer mechanism to a later lesson in the block.

claims.statement: Components of the endogenous beta-catenin destruction complex gathered towards Wnt-coated beads in 61 to 80 per cent of human colon epithelial cells carrying full-length APC, fell to about 30 per cent in a line expressing truncated APC, and Wnt-induced localisation was abolished where APC had been deleted.
claims.scope: The dependence of Wnt-induced destruction complex relocalisation on full-length APC, measured by localisation frequency in cultured human colon epithelial cells.
claims.uncertainty: Localisation frequencies in cultured cells, several of them colorectal cancer lines, scored by immunofluorescence against beads presenting a localised Wnt cue. This is an experimental arrangement rather than a crypt, and the percentages should be read as the result of that assay.

claims.statement: Because APC is both a component of the destruction complex and required for the complex to relocate towards a Wnt cue, a cell with damaged APC accumulates beta-catenin and runs the beta-catenin-dependent gene programme whether or not Wnt has arrived, so its output no longer tracks the Wnt concentration around it and it behaves as a cell at the crypt base would behave, at any height.
claims.scope: An interpretation of two sourced molecular findings in terms of positional reading, offered to show what the lesson's model explains about the consequence of losing APC.
claims.uncertainty: This is the lesson's inference and is labelled as such in the scene. The sources establish that APC loss impairs the destruction complex and permits beta-catenin accumulation, and that full-length APC is needed for relocalisation towards a Wnt cue; neither states the positional conclusion in these terms. The strength of the decoupling will depend on which part of APC is lost and on what else the cell carries. The lesson makes no claim that this alone produces a tumour, and defers that question to a later lesson in the block.

claims.statement: The colon renews every three to five days, with enterocytes replaced every four to five days.
claims.scope: The renewal interval of the colonic epithelium, used to argue that the instruction to divide is issued and withdrawn continuously in this tissue.
claims.uncertainty: A population-level interval for healthy tissue; individual cell lifespans vary and some epithelial cell types in the same tissue persist far longer. The figures match those used by PREM-BIO-001, PREM-BIO-002, PREM-BIO-003 and PREM-BIO-004 and are kept identical for block continuity. The argument that rapid renewal makes loss of the withdrawal step more consequential here than in a slowly renewing tissue is the lesson's own reasoning.

claims.statement: This lesson borrows five things from protein chemistry: that a protein has a definite shape which binding can change; that one protein can have separable parts doing separable jobs, so a shortened protein can lose one function and keep others; that a scaffold protein holds other proteins together without doing the chemistry itself, APC and Axin acting as the scaffolds here; that a protein can be tagged with ubiquitin and destroyed in the proteasome; and that a conserved amino acid is one unchanged at that position across many species.
claims.scope: The minimum protein vocabulary this lesson uses, assembled so that the unwritten prerequisite lesson on protein structure and folding is named rather than silently assumed.
claims.uncertainty: Each item is stated at the level this lesson needs and no further. The scaffold role of APC and Axin comes from the 2003 quantitative study, the separability of one protein's functions from the 2020 truncated-APC result, the ubiquitin-proteasome route from the 2025 review, and the conserved serine from the 2021 review. How a sequence produces a fold, and how binding at one site changes another, are not explained here and belong to PREM-09.03, which has no lesson yet.

claims.statement: Beta-catenin exists in a cell in more than one pool: a large and highly stable share is bound to membrane E-cadherin and takes no part in canonical Wnt signalling, and the study measuring the pathway's dynamics removed that fraction before analysis. The quantity the pathway's measurements report is free non-phosphorylated beta-catenin, the pool neither held in the destruction complex nor yet phosphorylated.
claims.scope: The distinction between the E-cadherin-bound pool and the signalling pool of beta-catenin, used to fix what every concentration figure in this lesson refers to.
claims.uncertainty: The source reports the E-cadherin-associated pool for the cells it studied and describes it as reported rather than newly measured there. This lesson uses the distinction only to name its own quantity precisely, and quantifies no pool other than the free non-phosphorylated one.

claims.statement: How Wnt binding reduces beta-catenin destruction is not settled. Relocalisation of some destruction complexes to the membrane accounts for part of it, but residual phosphorylating activity after Wnt stimulation comes mainly from complexes that did not move and that remain intact and active in the cytoplasm. Two further mechanisms are proposed: temporary inactivation of the complex by saturation with already-phosphorylated beta-catenin, and release of a partner that prevents the ubiquitin-attaching enzyme from docking. The question is described in the literature as controversial.
claims.scope: The unsettled state of the step between Wnt binding and reduced beta-catenin destruction, and the specific mechanisms under consideration.
claims.uncertainty: This claim records that the question is open, which is what the source states; it is not a claim that any one mechanism is correct. The lesson notes that everything downstream in the pack depends only on the reduction in destruction rate, which every proposed mechanism delivers, so no teaching in this pack turns on which is right.

claims.statement: Signalling receptors fall into broad architectural families: single-span plasma membrane receptors associated with tyrosine or serine/threonine kinase activities, proteins whose chain spans the membrane seven times, and intracellular receptors activated by ligands that cross the membrane. Receptor tyrosine kinases have an extracellular ligand-binding region, one transmembrane segment and an intracellular tyrosine kinase domain, and the family has more than fifty human members. G-protein-coupled receptors share a core of seven transmembrane helices forming three intracellular and three extracellular loops.
claims.scope: The architectural families of signalling receptors and the defining structure of receptor tyrosine kinases and of G-protein-coupled receptors, used to compare what each shape can do about this lesson's five jobs.
claims.uncertainty: The source's own grouping is by architecture and is not exhaustive: it treats ligand-gated ion channels only as targets of other signalling and does not present them as one of its families, so this lesson takes the direct-gating architecture from a separate source. Family membership is a structural classification and does not by itself fix the mechanism a given member runs, which is the point the Frizzled claims in this scene turn on.

claims.statement: Kinase-associated receptors are commonly activated by ligand-induced dimerisation or oligomerisation. Bringing the intracellular kinase domains together allows autophosphorylation in trans within the complex, which both raises the kinase activity and creates phosphorylated sequences that serve as docking sites for intracellular signalling proteins carrying SH2 or PTB domains.
claims.scope: The activation mechanism of receptor tyrosine kinases, used to show what an occupied receptor of this class makes available inside the cell.
claims.uncertainty: The source names exceptions to the activation-loop phosphorylation step, including Ret and the EGF receptor family, which this lesson does not go into. No rate, gain or stoichiometry is quoted for any step, and none is asserted here.

claims.statement: After ligand binding, kinase-associated receptors are internalised by clathrin-dependent or clathrin-independent routes, and internalisation has both positive and negative effects on signalling: receptors in endosomes are still active, and in some cases internalisation is necessary for the receptor to interact with its signalling partners. Signalling is interrupted when the endosomal pH falls far enough for the ligand to dissociate, at which point the receptors are dephosphorylated and recycle back to the cell surface.
claims.scope: The consequences of receptor internalisation for kinase-associated receptors, used to show that removing a receptor from the surface is not by itself a termination step.
claims.uncertainty: The source states that internalisation of receptor tyrosine kinases is induced by ligand binding while internalisation of serine/threonine receptors is constitutive; this lesson uses the receptor tyrosine kinase case. The source also describes an alternative fate for internalised receptors that this lesson does not follow. Nothing here is quantified.

claims.statement: Termination of G-protein-coupled receptor signalling proceeds through desensitisation. Receptor kinases known as GRKs phosphorylate only the activated, agonist-occupied form of the receptor, primarily in the carboxy-terminal tail; arrestin then binds, prevents interaction with the G protein, and promotes removal of the receptor from the cell surface by endocytosis. Second-messenger-regulated kinases such as PKA and PKC can also uncouple receptors from their G proteins.
claims.scope: How signalling through a G-protein-coupled receptor is switched off, used as the termination entry for that class in the receptor comparison.
claims.uncertainty: The source describes these as several well-understood mechanisms and does not rank them or give rates. That GRK phosphorylation is selective for the occupied receptor is the source's own statement; the observation that this makes the shut-off self-targeting is this lesson's reading of it.

claims.statement: Nuclear receptors are a superfamily of intracellular transcription factors activated by lipophilic ligands, and they differ from other receptors in not residing in the plasma membrane, which many of their ligands can cross. What distinguishes them from other kinds of receptor is the ability to mediate transcription without intermediate signalling cascades: they bind their target genes directly.
claims.scope: The defining feature of intracellular and nuclear receptors, used to show an architecture for which the transduction job does not arise.
claims.uncertainty: This is a statement about the number of stages between ligand binding and transcription and not about how long the response takes. The source gives no timescale for nuclear receptor responses, and this lesson explicitly refuses to convert the step count into a rate. The source also notes non-genomic effects of some nuclear receptors, which this lesson does not cover.

claims.statement: Notch receptors are single-pass transmembrane proteins whose canonical ligands are also membrane proteins present on neighbouring cells, so the receptor is normally triggered on cell-to-cell contact. Activation is a series of proteolytic events: ligand binding induces cleavage by ADAM metalloproteases at a site about twelve residues outside the transmembrane domain, and removal of the extracellular domain then permits an intramembrane cleavage by gamma-secretase that releases the intracellular domain, which carries a nuclear localisation sequence and travels to the nucleus to regulate transcription with a DNA-binding partner.
claims.scope: The architecture and activation mechanism of Notch, used both as an entry in the receptor comparison and as the reason a Notch input reports neighbours instead of position on an axis.
claims.uncertainty: The source gives no account of how Notch signalling is terminated, and this pack supplies none. It notes that signalling may also be induced in the ligand-bearing cell, which this lesson does not pursue. Nothing here is quantified, and no timescale is stated.

claims.statement: In chemosensory systems, ionotropic and metabotropic signalling pathways are described as fundamentally different in their temporal properties. The ionotropic route is usually faster, operating on a millisecond to sub-millisecond timescale, because ligand binding directly gates the ion channel. Metabotropic receptors have a longer latency, from a few tens to several hundred milliseconds, because second messengers must be produced and secondary effectors activated; as a consequence of those downstream effects, metabotropic signalling can have a much longer duration, from a few seconds to several minutes.
claims.scope: The only timescale comparison between receptor architectures that this lesson could source, established in insect and mammalian chemoreception and used only for the direct-gating and second-messenger architectures.
claims.uncertainty: The figures come from a review of chemoreception and are scoped to chemosensory systems; the lesson says so where it uses them and does not present them as general values. The source reports latency and duration as two different quantities, and this lesson keeps them apart instead of collapsing them into a single notion of speed. The source says nothing about receptor tyrosine kinases or intracellular receptors, so no timescale is asserted for those, and no source consulted places all of the compared architectures on one timescale.

claims.statement: Frizzled receptors share an architecture of an extracellular cysteine-rich domain, a hydrophilic linker region, a seven-transmembrane domain and an intracellular carboxy-terminal region, and are assigned to class F of the G-protein-coupled receptors. On the grounds of those seven-transmembrane segments, evidence for coupling between Frizzleds and G proteins, and substantial structural differences from class A, B and C receptors, Frizzleds were grouped separately in the IUPHAR GPCR database as the class FZD within the GPCR superfamily. Frizzleds retain conserved cysteines in extracellular loops 1 and 2 and charged residues at the ends of intracellular loop 3 that are associated with receptor-to-G-protein coupling, but they lack the DRY motif at the carboxy-terminal end of the third transmembrane domain, a feature known to matter for G protein coupling and specificity.
claims.scope: The domain architecture of Frizzled receptors and the formal basis for placing them in class F of the GPCRs, together with the structural features they keep and the one they lack.
claims.uncertainty: The classification is a formal database assignment made on stated grounds and is not the same as a demonstration that these receptors signal through heterotrimeric G proteins; the separate contested claim in this scene carries that question. The DRY motif statement is reported by the IUPHAR review citing earlier work.

claims.statement: Whether Frizzled receptors should be classified strictly as G-protein-coupled receptors is disputed in the literature. A 2025 review states that the exact contributions of the seven-transmembrane domain to signal transduction are contentious and that, because Frizzleds exhibit limited direct G-protein coupling, there is debate over whether they should be classified strictly as GPCRs or as part of a broader receptor family with hybrid functionalities. The 2014 IUPHAR review states that Frizzled and G protein coupling remains to be fully explored while describing the basic observation supporting the nature of Frizzleds as GPCRs as compelling. A 2021 structural study argues that, given how much receptor topology varies across the classes that do couple G proteins, it is not as controversial as it would first seem that Frizzleds and Smoothened adopt different conformations while activating the same G proteins.
claims.scope: The disputed status of Frizzled's membership of the GPCR class, reported as a live disagreement between named sources and used to teach that architecture fixes family more securely than it fixes mechanism.
claims.uncertainty: This claim asserts that the question is disputed, which the sources establish; it asserts no resolution, and this pack takes no position. The three sources do not weigh equally on one side: the 2025 review frames the classification itself as debated, while the IUPHAR review and the 2021 study both lean toward Frizzleds being genuine GPCRs and hedge about mechanism instead of membership. Nothing taught elsewhere in this pack depends on the answer, because the Wnt chain traced in scene 2 invokes no heterotrimeric G protein at any step.

claims.statement: The E3 ubiquitin ligases ZNRF3 and RNF43 ubiquitinate Frizzled receptors, targeting them for lysosomal degradation, and this acts as a negative feedback mechanism that terminates Wnt signalling.
claims.scope: A receptor-level route by which Wnt signalling is terminated, distinguished in the scene from the intracellular termination described earlier in the pack.
claims.uncertainty: The source states this as a negative feedback mechanism without quantifying its contribution or its timescale, and no figure is asserted. This route operates on receptor availability and does not replace the account of termination given for the beta-catenin arm, where the destruction complex runs continuously; the scene says the two act at different places and this pack does not compare their magnitudes.

claims.statement: BMP signalling in the colonic crypt is highest at the top of the crypt and decreases towards the base, forming a gradient inverse to that of WNT signalling, and this gradient is maintained by BMP antagonists such as Noggin and Gremlin secreted by mesenchymal cells at the base of the crypt. A review of the intestinal niche further states that BMP represses Wnt signalling and is expressed in an opposing gradient along the crypt-villus axis, with the highest BMP signalling in the cells at the luminal surface.
claims.scope: The existence and direction of a second, anti-parallel signalling gradient along the crypt axis, and the reported repression of Wnt by BMP.
claims.uncertainty: The colonic review states the gradient direction for the normal colon without attributing it to a species, and the references beneath that paragraph are mouse studies. The statement that BMP represses Wnt, and the mechanism behind it, come from the second review, which is explicitly about the small intestine and whose evidence is mouse genetics and organoids. So the direction of the gradient is on firmer ground for the human colon than the repression mechanism is, and the scene says which is which.

claims.statement: Notch signalling is active in the stem cell niche and the transit-amplifying compartment of the colonic crypt. NOTCH1 to NOTCH4 are activated by Delta-like and Jagged ligands expressed on adjacent cells; cleavage releases the Notch intracellular domain, which enters the nucleus and activates target genes including HES1. HES1 represses ATOH1, a master regulator of secretory lineage differentiation, and the effect is to promote the absorptive colonocyte fate while inhibiting differentiation into goblet, enteroendocrine and tuft cells. A review of the intestinal niche describes this as the binary cell fate decision between the secretory and absorptive lineages.
claims.scope: What the Notch input contributes in the crypt, used to show that a contact-dependent signal can make a distinction the axial gradient cannot.
claims.uncertainty: The colonic review states these mechanisms for the normal colon without species attribution, resting on mouse and general pathway references. The binary fate-decision phrasing comes from a figure caption in the second review, which is about mouse small intestine. That review attributes the Notch ligands to Paneth cells, a small-intestinal type the colonic review states the colon lacks, so this pack does not carry that detail. The colonic review also swaps the secretory and absorptive labels in an earlier section; this claim follows its section 4.5, which states them correctly.

claims.statement: The direction of the relationship between Wnt and Notch in the crypt is not resolved by the reviews consulted here. One review states that the Wnt pathway synergises with Notch signalling to sustain undifferentiated and proliferative stem and progenitor cells, and in the same section reports that inhibiting Notch with blocking antibodies converted Lgr5-expressing intestinal stem cells into secretory cells and depleted the stem cell pool, coinciding with upregulation of the Wnt pathway, with the phenotype rescued by repressing Wnt, which the authors say suggests opposing and interconnected activities. The other review states only that Notch interacts with other pathways such as WNT, and neither offers a mechanism for the interaction in the normal colon.
claims.scope: The state of the evidence on whether Wnt and Notch cooperate or oppose one another in the crypt, carried as unresolved.
claims.uncertainty: Both the synergy statement and the opposition reading sit in one section of one review and trace back to the same primary study, which was not itself retrieved by this pack, so the two are not independent. The review does not reconcile them and this pack does not either. The evidence is mouse small intestine; no human colonic demonstration was found. An assessment item in this pack is keyed so that stating either direction as settled is the error it catches.

claims.statement: A crypt cell is acted on by several signalling pathways at once. A 2025 review of the colonic crypt states that the coordinated interplay of WNT, Notch, BMP and FGF signalling is essential for maintaining colonic epithelial homeostasis, and that disruption of the balance among these pathways can result in aberrant proliferation, impaired differentiation and defective epithelial renewal. A review of the intestinal niche states that intestinal stem cells interpret the signals derived from the niche to balance cell loss against replenishment.
claims.scope: The general statement that crypt cells read multiple signalling inputs, used as the premise of the cross-talk scene.
claims.uncertainty: Both statements are summary framings in review articles and neither is a measurement. Neither review quantifies how the inputs are combined, and the colonic review's summary sentence cites a cancer stemness review and a tumour therapy-resistance review rather than normal-crypt studies. No claim is made here about the arithmetic of combination, which the pack treats separately and as its own reasoning.

claims.statement: Adding a second input does not automatically add positional information. An input that varies along the same axis as Wnt and in the opposite direction is largely a restatement of the Wnt reading, because both are functions of the single coordinate of height, in the same way that thresholds nested on one gradient are redundant with one another. A contact-dependent input is not redundant in that way, because what it reports is which cells are adjacent and it is not a function of height; that is why two cells at the same crypt height can take different fates.
claims.scope: This pack's own reasoning about what a second signalling input can and cannot contribute to a cell's estimate of its position, used to connect the cross-talk scene to the information bound established earlier.
claims.uncertainty: This is reasoning applied to sourced facts and not a quoted finding. No source consulted counts bits for the crypt, measures what any second input contributes, or states that BMP and Wnt readings are informationally redundant, and no figure is asserted anywhere in the scene. The redundancy argument is qualitative and would not hold in full if the two gradients had independent noise or differed in shape, which this pack cannot check; the scene says what a second reading of one coordinate could still plausibly offer. The claim rests on the sourced anti-parallel direction of the BMP gradient, the sourced contact-dependence of Notch, and the sourced result that a single threshold read of a monotonic gradient carries at most one bit.

terms.definition: A molecule released by one cell whose presence and amount change what another cell does. The everyday sense of a signal, as in a traffic signal or a hand signal, keeps the part that matters: something is sent so that something else will change its behaviour. What biology adds is that the sender and receiver are cells and the message is a molecule, so the message carries no content beyond how much of it there is and where it binds. A signal does not name a state of affairs; the receiving cell's machinery supplies all of the interpretation. Distinct from a signal sequence, which is part of a protein's own chain and addresses the inside of one cell.

An extracellular signal molecule considered in its capacity as the thing that binds a receptor. Signal and ligand can pick out the same molecule; the word ligand puts the emphasis on the binding event rather than on the sending.

A protein that binds a particular signal and, as a consequence of binding it, changes what it does. A cell-surface receptor sits in the membrane with a part outside the cell and a part inside, so that a binding event on the outside becomes a change on the inside. In this lesson the Wnt receptor is a pair of proteins working together, Frizzled with LRP5/6, which is a reminder that one receptor function need not mean one receptor molecule.

The conversion of a binding event outside a cell into a change inside it. Cell-surface receptors act as signal transducers: they turn an extracellular ligand-binding event into intracellular signals that alter the target cell's behaviour. Transduction is a change of medium rather than a change of message, which is why the word is borrowed from engineering.

The return of a cell towards its unstimulated state when a signal is withdrawn. Termination is part of what makes a signal informative rather than a switch thrown once, and it is often supplied by the continual turnover of the molecules the signal alters. In the canonical Wnt pathway termination needs nothing new to be built, because the machinery that destroys the output is running at all times and simply resumes its usual effect.

A systematic difference in the amount of a substance across space, so that the concentration at one place differs from the concentration at another. In this lesson the gradient runs along the length of a crypt and the quantity that varies is a Wnt protein. The word describes the profile and not its cause: a falling profile can be produced by spreading and breakdown, or by handover between cells combined with dilution, and which of those builds the crypt gradient is unsettled. PREM-BIO-003's proton gradient is a difference of this kind across a membrane rather than along a tissue, and the two are separate cases of the same idea.

What a cell can determine about where it sits from a quantity it can measure locally. Treating it as information is what makes it countable: telling apart 32 positions demands five binary distinctions, and a single gene reading a single threshold on a gradient that falls in one direction supplies one, distinguishing two regions and no more. A gradient therefore supplies coarse zones rather than coordinates, and real systems exceed that ceiling by letting genes influence one another and by using graded expression rather than on-or-off calls.

A substance that spreads from a source and specifies what cells become according to its local concentration. Wnt in the colonic crypt fits the second half of that description comfortably: what a cell becomes does depend on how much reaches it. Whether it fits the first half in the classical sense of diffusive spreading is an open question, because Wnt proteins are lipid-modified and their mode of travel is debated. This lesson uses the word for the role Wnt plays and not as a claim about how it moves.

A family of secreted signalling proteins, and in this lesson the signal that reports height in the colonic crypt. Mesenchymal cells near the crypt base secrete them and cells further away do not, so Wnt activity falls progressively up the crypt axis. Wnt proteins carry a lipid modification that makes them hydrophobic, which is required for their secretion and is also what makes their travel through watery extracellular space difficult to explain.

The assembly that keeps free beta-catenin scarce in a cell receiving no Wnt. It includes APC, Axin and the kinases CK1A and GSK3B; beta-catenin is drawn in, phosphorylated, then tagged with ubiquitin and destroyed in the proteasome. Wnt binding reduces the rate of that destruction, so the pathway raises its output by interfering with destruction instead of increasing production. How the reduction happens is not settled: some complexes relocate to the membrane while remaining assembled, but the complexes that stay in the cytosol remain active, and saturation of the complex or blocking of the ubiquitin-tagging step are both proposed to account for the rest.

The protein whose amount carries the Wnt signal inside the cell. It exists in more than one pool, and only one of them matters here: a large, highly stable share is bound to E-cadherin at the membrane and takes no part in canonical Wnt signalling. **Free beta-catenin**, the quantity every figure in this lesson refers to, is the pool neither held inside the destruction complex nor yet phosphorylated; sources also call it free non-phosphorylated beta-catenin, or available beta-catenin. It is made continuously and, without Wnt, destroyed continuously, so its level reports the balance of synthesis against destruction. Free beta-catenin that escapes destruction enters the nucleus and acts with TCF and LEF.

A large scaffolding protein of the beta-catenin destruction complex, present at about 100 nanomolar in the system where the pathway was quantified. It has two roles in this lesson: it belongs to the complex that marks beta-catenin for destruction, and full-length APC is required for that complex to reorient towards a localised Wnt cue. Damage to it therefore leaves beta-catenin accumulating whether or not Wnt has arrived. The gene encoding it carries the same name.

A protein that binds to DNA or to a DNA-bound partner and changes whether nearby genes are transcribed. TCF and LEF are the transcription factors that beta-catenin partners in this pathway, which is how a concentration outside the cell becomes a change in which genes are read.

A relay chain that contains multiple amplification steps. The definition matters because the word is often applied to any multi-step pathway and the amplification then read back out of the label. Whether a given chain earns the word is a question to answer with evidence about its steps: phototransduction has two identifiable multiplying steps, while the canonical Wnt pathway's identifiable catalytic steps sit on the arm that destroys its output. This is the narrower of two usages. The term is also applied loosely to any multi-step relay, so a source calling a pathway a cascade is not by itself evidence that the pathway amplifies.

A step at which one activated molecule causes many molecules to be activated, converted or modified, so the number affected grows along the chain. Amplification is a property of individual steps rather than of pathways as a whole, and a pathway can contain a strongly amplifying step while showing a small change in output, when that step sits on the arm removing the response. Gains are also reported in more than one kind of unit: a per-event catalytic tally (molecules consumed per input event) is a different quantity from a ratio of two steady-state levels, and the two cannot be divided into one another. In the canonical Wnt pathway the catalytic steps belong to the kinases that mark beta-catenin for destruction.

A cell with the capacity to self-renew and to produce differentiated progeny. The definition is about capacity rather than continuous activity: some stem-cell populations are quiescent until activated, while others cycle actively. In this lesson the term names the cells at the crypt base, which are the cells with the highest Wnt activity and whose gene programme this lesson's pathway switches on.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-001 defines stem cell for this course and this lesson keeps that meaning without alteration: capacity to self-renew and to produce differentiated progeny, with capacity distinguished from continuous division. Nothing is narrowed or extended here. What this lesson adds is the mechanism by which the crypt-base population's programme is switched on, which PREM-BIO-001 deferred to a later lesson in the block.

terms.definition: A cell-surface receptor built around a core of seven transmembrane helices, which form three intracellular and three extracellular loops. Binding on the outside is registered by a separate protein on the inner face of the membrane, so the receptor itself neither conducts ions nor performs the chemistry of the response. Signalling through one is switched off by desensitisation: receptor kinases phosphorylate the ligand-occupied form, arrestin binds, the interaction with the G protein is blocked, and the receptor is taken off the surface by endocytosis. Frizzled is assigned to class F of this group, and whether Frizzleds should be classified strictly as members is disputed in the literature.

A cell-surface receptor with an extracellular ligand-binding region, a single transmembrane segment, and an intracellular region carrying a tyrosine kinase domain. Ligand binding brings two receptors together; the juxtaposed kinase domains phosphorylate one another, which raises their activity and creates phosphorylated sequences on the receptor's own tail that intracellular proteins with SH2 or PTB domains can dock onto. What the cell gains is an assembly point built out of the receptor. The family has more than fifty human members.

A receptor in which the ligand-binding site and an ion channel belong to one protein, so that binding opens the channel directly and ions flow. Nothing has to be synthesised and no separate messenger has to be found; what crosses the membrane is charge. Receptors of this kind are also called ionotropic, in contrast with metabotropic receptors that work through second messengers, though in the insect chemosensory literature Ionotropic Receptor also names one particular gene family, which is a narrower use of the word and not a synonym for this entry.

A member of a superfamily of intracellular transcription factors activated by lipophilic ligands. These receptors do not sit in the plasma membrane, and their ligands cross it unaided, so no binding event on the outside has to be converted into one on the inside. What sets them apart from other receptors is that they mediate transcription without intermediate signalling cascades, binding their target genes directly. A nuclear receptor is one kind of intracellular receptor; the broader term also covers intracellular receptors that are not transcription factors, so the two are not interchangeable.

The receptor that binds Wnt ligands, working together with LRP5/6. Its chain crosses the membrane seven times, and it carries an extracellular cysteine-rich domain, a hydrophilic linker, the seven-transmembrane domain, and an intracellular carboxy-terminal region. Frizzleds are assigned to class F of the G-protein-coupled receptors and were grouped in the IUPHAR database as class FZD within that superfamily. Whether they should be classified strictly as G-protein-coupled receptors is disputed, and this lesson reports the dispute without resolving it.

The condition of a cell being acted on by more than one signalling pathway at once, so that its behaviour is a joint function of several inputs instead of one. In the colonic crypt a cell sits in a Wnt gradient falling from the base, a BMP gradient falling from the top, and a contact-dependent Notch input carried on its neighbours' surfaces. Reading several inputs does not by itself supply more positional information: an input that varies along the same axis is largely a restatement of the first, while an input that is not a function of position can make distinctions the axis cannot.

Sources

Eighteen sources are recorded in references.json and every one was retrieved and read directly, twelve by the original authoring run and six more by the coverage addition recorded below. Every asserted fact in the scenes maps to a claim in claims.json, and every claim appears in a learner-visible {source-note} in each scene where it is used.

Sources by host:

  • pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov (sixteen sources). Recorded allowed in the source-access ledger, whose entry cites robots.txt carrying Allow: /articles/. Nguyen, Lausten & Boman 2025 on the colonic crypt; Parker & Neufeld 2020 on APC and destruction complex recruitment in human colonocytes; Lee, Salic, Krüger, Heinrich & Kirschner 2003 on the quantitative Wnt pathway; Goentoro & Kirschner 2009 on fold-change readout; Mehta, Hingole & Chaudhary 2021 on Wnt secretion mechanisms; Hillenbrand, Gerland & Tkačik 2016 on positional information beyond the French flag model; Tostevin, ten Wolde & Howard 2007 on the fundamental limits to position determination; van der Wath, Gardiner, Burgess & Smith 2013 on crypt geometry; Baker and colleagues 2014 on crypt migration speed; Mukherjee, Dhar, Stathos, Schaffer & Kane 2018 on how Wnt influences destruction complex activity. Added by the coverage run: Heldin, Lu, Evans & Gutkind 2016 on signals and receptors; Silbering & Benton 2010 on ionotropic and metabotropic mechanisms in chemoreception; Martinez-Marin, Stroman, Fulton & Pruitt 2025 on Frizzled receptors; Dijksterhuis, Petersen & Schulte 2014, IUPHAR Review 3 on WNT/Frizzled signalling; Turku, Schihada, Kozielewicz, Bowin & Schulte 2021 on residue 6.43 in class F GPCRs; Spit, Koo & Maurice 2018 on intestinal niche signals.
  • www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov (two sources, both NCBI Bookshelf chapters of Molecular Biology of the Cell, 4th edition). This host is recorded restricted in the ledger because robots.txt disallows the legacy /pmc/articles route for unnamed agents. That restriction does not reach the Bookshelf chapter route. This run retrieved and read the full robots.txt before access and confirmed that the wildcard User-agent: * block disallows /pmc/articles and a set of query and tool paths, that its only books rule is Disallow: /books/?term=, which covers the search query route and not chapter pages, and that the file names no AI or LLM crawler and carries no rule applying to this agent. The additional detail the first run established about the Bookshelf route is recorded in the agentAccess notes of the two affected source records instead of in the shared ledger, because a second agent was authoring in the same worktree concurrently and an unnecessary write to a shared file risks clobbering its append. Two access observations from the coverage run are recorded here because they concern rate and not rights, and so do not change either ledger verdict. First, www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov returned an "Access Denied" page citing possible misuse after a burst of requests, and stayed blocked across a backoff, so no Bookshelf chapter was reopened by that run and no new fact was taken from either Bookshelf source. The receptor-class material was sourced from PubMed Central instead. Second, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov served a reCAPTCHA challenge on one article during a rapid sequence of fetches. That challenge was not circumvented in any way; the run waited and retried the plain URL once, which succeeded. Future authors should pace requests to these hosts.

No source was retrieved from a domain marked excluded or human-only. No login, paywall, access control or bot challenge was bypassed anywhere in either run.

Sources under restrictive licences

Seven sources carry licences that permit no reuse of expression, or state a licence this pack has chosen not to rely on, and every one of them is used for unprotectable fact only:

  • source-goentoro-fold-change — Molecular Cell, © 2009 Elsevier Inc., all rights reserved, read as a PubMed Central author manuscript. Only the fold-change range, the span of absolute concentrations, and the authors' stated proposal are taken.
  • source-baker-crypt-dynamics — CC BY-NC-ND, so both the non-commercial and the no-derivatives terms bar reuse. Only the measured migration speed is taken.
  • source-mukherjee-destruction-complex — CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, same bar. Only the competing proposed mechanisms, the partial nature of relocalisation, and the existence of an E-cadherin-bound beta-catenin pool are taken.
  • source-heldin-signals-receptors — Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press. The article page carries no Creative Commons licence and no open-access grant, so only the receptor architectures and their activation and shut-off mechanisms are taken.
  • source-silbering-chemoreception-timing — © 2010 European Molecular Biology Organization, no Creative Commons licence on the page. Only the ionotropic and metabotropic timescale figures are taken.
  • source-dijksterhuis-iuphar-frizzled — a bare British Pharmacological Society copyright line and no Creative Commons licence. Only the IUPHAR classification, the retained and missing structural features, and the review's own characterisation of the evidence are taken.
  • source-martinez-marin-frizzled — the page states a Creative Commons Attribution licence but names no version and links no versioned deed, so this pack does not rely on the grant and treats it as facts-only like the entries above.

The two NCBI Bookshelf chapters are under publisher copyright and are likewise used for fact only.

Known limitations of this pack

These are recorded deliberately. An honest gap is more useful to a reviewer than a confident guess.

1. The protein prerequisite has no lesson. This outcome declares two graph prerequisites, and one of them, topic-biomolecules-proteins (PREM-09.03, "Protein structure and folding"), has no published lesson anywhere in the corpus. That gap bites directly on this material, because a receptor is a protein and what a receptor does on binding a ligand is change shape. This pack does not re-teach protein structure and folding and does not paper over the absence. Scene 1 names the dependency explicitly, says that PREM-09.03 will own it, says it should be read first once it exists, and reduces what this lesson needs to a single stated sentence: a protein has a definite shape, and binding something can change it. Nothing downstream in the pack requires more protein chemistry than that. What a learner will therefore not get here is any account of how a sequence produces a fold, why a binding site has a particular geometry, or how binding at one end of a protein moves the other end.

2. No receptor copy number. The noise argument in scene 4 depends on a cell counting randomly arriving molecules at a finite number of receptors. No published figure for the number of Wnt receptors on a human colonic crypt cell was found, and none is supplied. Scene 4 says so in a scoping callout rather than substituting a plausible number.

3. The noise limit is transferred from a subcellular model. source-tostevin-position-limits models gradients used for positioning inside a single cell, of the kind bacteria use to find their own middle, not a tissue-scale gradient across an epithelium. The pack transfers only the structure of the argument and the square-root scaling of precision with averaging time, both consequences of molecules arriving at random, and states the limitation where it is used.

4. The positional information figure is from an insect. The 4.2-bit estimate is for the Drosophila gap genes, in a syncytium of nuclei sharing a cytoplasm. No equivalent measurement for the human colonic crypt was found. The scene states this and does not present the figure as the crypt's value.

5. The Wnt gain figure is a model of a frog extract. The approximately sixfold rise in free non-phosphorylated beta-catenin comes from a fitted model supported by measurements in Xenopus egg extracts, not from a measurement inside a human crypt cell, and the comparison with phototransduction sets a modelled figure beside textbook figures from a different system. Both scenes that use it say so. The comparison is offered to show that measured gains differ by orders of magnitude, not to rank the two pathways precisely.

6. Gradient formation is unsettled and is left unsettled. How a Wnt gradient forms is genuinely open, and scene 7 presents the competing readings with the observation behind each rather than choosing one. The short-range lateral transcytosis result is reported in a 2021 review of a 2016 primary study; the primary study was not itself retrieved, and the pack attributes the finding to work reported in the review rather than presenting it first-hand. That work is in mouse small intestine and concerns Wnt3, whereas this block follows the human colonic crypt, where the same review identifies the mesenchyme as the ligand source.

7. The destruction complex composition is stated non-exhaustively on purpose. source-nguyen-colonic-crypt lists Dishevelled among the complex's components. Dishevelled's placement is described differently across the literature, so this pack names only APC, Axin, CK1A and GSK3B, says the complex "includes" them, and records the divergence in scene 2's source note and in the claim's uncertainty field. Nothing taught here depends on settling it.

8. The positional interpretation of APC loss is an inference. That a cell with damaged APC reports the crypt base at any height is this pack's reading of two sourced molecular findings, not a quoted conclusion. claim-apc-loss-decouples-readout records it as support: inference at medium confidence, and the scene labels it as an interpretation.

9. Amplification is the one job of five not traced through Wnt itself. The outcome asks for reception, transduction, amplification, response and termination. Four of those are traced through the crypt's own Wnt pathway. Amplification is traced through vertebrate phototransduction, whose per-step figures are published, and through a composite pathway written for scene 8's audit. The reason is stated in scene 6 rather than hidden: no source consulted here reports a per-event catalytic gain for any step of the canonical Wnt pathway, and the transcriptional step in particular is left unaudited because no figure was found that this pack could stand behind. What the pack does establish about Wnt is where its multiplying steps sit, namely on the arm that destroys the output, and what its output ratio is. What it cannot state is by how much any single Wnt step multiplies.

10. The two gain figures are not commensurable, and the pack says so instead of comparing them. An earlier draft divided phototransduction's tally of more than 100,000 molecules per absorbed photon by the Wnt pathway's roughly sixfold change and reported a four-orders-of-magnitude difference. That comparison is invalid: the first is a per-event catalytic count with units, the second a dimensionless ratio of two steady-state concentrations. Scene 6 now names the error explicitly, an assessment item uses the invalid division as its most attractive distractor, and no numerical comparison between the two pathways' gains is asserted anywhere in the pack.

11. How Wnt slows destruction is unsettled, and the pack carries all the candidates. Scene 2 originally joined "the complex is recruited to the membrane" and "available beta-catenin rises" with an "and", leaving the causal step blank. It now reports what the sources support: relocation of some complexes is real and is the authors' proposal, relocation alone does not account for the loss of activity because the complexes that stay in the cytosol remain active, and saturation of the complex or interruption of the ubiquitin-tagging step are both proposed for the remainder. The literature calls the question controversial and the pack does not resolve it. Nothing taught in the pack depends on which mechanism wins, because every candidate delivers the same reduction in destruction rate.

12. No timescale comparison across receptor classes. Scene 3 compares receptor architectures by what crosses the membrane and by how each is switched off, and it deliberately has no speed column. The only timescale figure this pack could source is the ionotropic against metabotropic comparison in source-silbering-chemoreception-timing, which was established in insect and mammalian chemosensory systems and reports nothing about receptor tyrosine kinases or intracellular receptors. No source consulted places all of the compared architectures on one timescale. The scene therefore states the chemosensory figures inside their scope, keeps the source's latency and duration apart instead of merging them into a single notion of speed, and refuses in prose to convert a count of stages into a rate. An assessment item is keyed on exactly that refusal.

13. Frizzled's membership of the GPCR class is contested and is left contested. The pack reports the formal IUPHAR placement with the three grounds given for it, and reports the dispute with named sources on each side, and takes no position. The three sources do not weigh equally: only source-martinez-marin-frizzled frames the classification itself as debated, while source-dijksterhuis-iuphar-frizzled and source-turku-class-f both lean toward Frizzleds being genuine GPCRs and hedge about mechanism instead of membership. The claim's uncertainty field says so, so that a reviewer is not left to infer a balance the sources do not have. Nothing elsewhere in the pack depends on the answer: the Wnt chain traced in scene 2 invokes no heterotrimeric G protein at any step, and that is stated in the scene.

14. The cross-talk mechanisms are better evidenced in mouse small intestine than in human colon. source-nguyen-colonic-crypt states the BMP gradient direction and the Notch fate mechanism for the normal colon without attributing either to a species, and the references beneath those two paragraphs are mouse studies and general pathway reviews. source-spit-crypt-niche is explicitly about the small intestine, is organised on a crypt-to-villus axis, notes itself that the colon has crypts and no villi, and reports no human crypt data; its evidence is mouse genetics and organoids. Scene 5 carries a scoping callout saying which statement rests on which, and deliberately omits that review's attribution of the Notch ligands to Paneth cells, a small-intestinal cell type the colonic review states the colon lacks. source-nguyen-colonic-crypt also swaps the secretory and absorptive labels in its section 2.1; this pack uses its section 4.5, which states them correctly, and records the discrepancy in that source's rights-basis note so no later author copies the error.

15. The information argument about combining inputs is reasoning, not measurement. Scene 5 argues that a second gradient running the other way along the same axis is largely redundant with Wnt, while a contact-dependent input is not. That argument is claim-combining-inputs-not-additive, carried at support: inference and medium confidence. No source consulted counts bits for the crypt, measures what any second input contributes, or states that the Wnt and BMP readings are informationally redundant. The scene labels the argument as the lesson's own where it appears, names the conditions under which it would weaken, and asserts no figure. The assessment item built on it asks for the reasoning and explicitly does not ask for a number.

16. The direction of the Wnt and Notch relationship is unresolved and is carried that way. One review states that Wnt synergises with Notch to sustain undifferentiated proliferative stem and progenitor cells, and in the same section reports an experiment its authors read as showing opposing and interconnected activities. Both statements trace back to a single primary study, which this pack did not retrieve, so they are not independent, and the review reconciles neither. The other review says only that Notch interacts with pathways such as Wnt, and neither gives a mechanism for the normal colon. The pack states both readings and settles nothing, and the short-answer item is keyed so that asserting either direction as settled is the error it catches.

Coverage addition: receptor classes and cross-talk

An independent academic review found that this pack traced one canonical Wnt example and covered neither the receptor-class comparison nor the cross-talk that the syllabus outcome BIO-124 asks for, and that an earlier version of this file had declared a receptor-class survey out of scope. That finding is correct and this section records how it was closed. The out-of-scope declaration has been removed from the scope exclusions above.

Two scenes were added and the existing seven were left as they were, apart from renumbering.

  • Scene 3, "What kind of receptor is Frizzled?" (content/03-what-kind-of-receptor.md, 11 minutes). It sits immediately after the scene that introduces the receptor. It compares ligand-gated ion channels, receptor tyrosine kinases, G-protein-coupled receptors, Notch, and intracellular or nuclear receptors by what each architecture predicts, ties each back to the pack's five jobs, and places Frizzled among them with its class F assignment and the dispute over that assignment. It was written as its own scene instead of a section inside scene 2 because scene 2's structure is a march through the five jobs traced in one pathway, and a comparison across pathways interrupts it.
  • Scene 5, "Reading more than one input" (content/05-reading-more-than-one-input.md, 10 minutes). It sits immediately after the scene that bounds what one gradient can specify, because it is the answer to the limit that scene establishes. It covers the anti-parallel BMP gradient, the contact-dependent Notch input, what the sources do and do not settle about Wnt with Notch, and the argument that combining inputs does not automatically add positional information.

The scenes were inserted in reading order, so the seven existing scenes were renumbered and every numeric scene cross-reference in the pack's prose, in this file, and in the content filenames was updated to match. No existing teaching content was rewritten.

Also added: fifteen claims in claims.json and six sources in references.json; three assessment items and one rubric; six glossary terms; two objectives in lesson.json; and the Notch and BMP pointers in the locator and rights-basis note of source-nguyen-colonic-crypt, which the coverage run re-read for that purpose. estimatedMinutes rises from 115 to 136.

Nothing the pack already taught was contradicted. In particular the addition preserves the record that how membrane recruitment of the destruction complex leads to the rise in beta-catenin is unsettled, that noise can only subtract from positional information, that a binary threshold carries at most one bit, and that "cascade" is a convention and not an exclusive definition. Scene 3's account of Frizzled being removed by ZNRF3 and RNF43 is stated as a receptor-level control acting alongside, and not in place of, the intracellular termination account in scene 2, and the scene says the two act at different places without comparing their magnitudes.

One thing was wanted and left out for lack of a source. A speed column for the receptor comparison was intended and is not there, for the reason recorded as limitation 12.

The instructionsDigest in lesson.json was not re-stamped by the coverage run. It remains a genuine SHA-256 over the original authoring run's disclosed task payload and does not cover the coverage run's own instructions, which are not represented by any digest in this pack. That is recorded here instead of being papered over, and it is the operator's to resolve alongside the other RUNTIME-STAMPED provenance fields.

Deliberate scope exclusions

  • Non-canonical Wnt signalling. The planar cell polarity and calcium branches are not covered. The outcome is served by tracing one pathway completely instead of surveying several partially.
  • Second messengers. Scene 4 compares receptor architectures and scene 8 uses phototransduction as its high-gain case, but no systematic account of cyclic AMP, cyclic GMP, calcium or the phosphoinositides is given, and none is needed by anything this pack asserts.
  • Cancer mechanism. Scene 9 sets up topic-cell-biology-cell-death-cancer (PREM-05.10) and stops. How a decoupled readout becomes a tumour, what else must go wrong, and anything about staging, screening, prognosis or treatment are outside this pack.
  • Gradient shape from first principles. No calculation of a concentration profile from a diffusion coefficient is attempted, because scene 7 establishes that the mechanism of spread is the disputed part.
  • Membrane structure and fluidity. Owned by PREM-BIO-004 and adopted rather than re-taught.

Block continuity

Figures shared with earlier packs in this block are kept identical: the crypt at about 32 cells along its length and about 22 around its circumference with roughly 700 cells, a mean cell radius of 5 micrometres, upward migration at around 4 micrometres per hour in the lower half of the crypt, and colonic renewal every three to five days with enterocytes replaced every four to five days. The stem cell glossary entry adopts PREM-BIO-001's definition and declares alignment with relation adopt. PREM-BIO-001's claim-crypt-architecture recorded that the mechanism by which a cell reads its position was the subject of a later lesson in this block; this pack is that lesson, and scene 2 supplies the mechanism it deferred.

Educational and medical boundary

Every clinical statement in this pack is scoped as teaching material. Scene 8 and scene 9 each carry an explicit teaching example, not medical advice boundary callout. The pack describes no patient and no case history, names no drug, dose or regimen, makes no recommendation, and offers nothing that could support a diagnosis, a prognosis, a screening decision or a treatment choice. The colorectal cancer mutation frequency quoted in scene 9 is a population figure from a review and is labelled as such; it is not a personal risk and says nothing about any individual. Two claims are flagged health-sensitive in claims.json.

Provenance

The accountable principal is VSBDev (github:VSBDev), consistent with the other packs in this block. This run was instructed not to execute any gh command, so the identity was not re-verified against the GitHub API in this run and is carried from the block's existing published packs rather than guessed.

Agent system, provider, model, version and run identifier are recorded in lesson.json as the literal RUNTIME-STAMPED for the operator to stamp before review. None of them is asserted by this run, because this run could not obtain them without inventing them.

The instructionsDigest is a genuine SHA-256 over the exact disclosed UTF-8 material task payload supplied to this run, including its final newline. It could not be emitted as RUNTIME-STAMPED because site/schemas/lesson.schema.json constrains the field to the pattern ^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$, so a real digest is recorded rather than a placeholder that would fail schema validation. The digest covers only that payload and excludes hidden provider and system instructions that cannot be exported.

Governance status

This pack is an authoring candidate. status is draft, sourceConfidence is pending-review, and every claim in claims.json carries reviewStatus: pending-review. No review or adjudication artifact was created by this run, and none exists in this pack. Nothing here has been reviewed, approved, published or merged, and this pack claims no coverage of its outcome until independent review and adjudication say otherwise.

Adjudication repairs to the 0.1.0 candidate

The academic review returned request-changes with five major findings, two minor and one verification note; the learning-design review approved with five notes. All seven actionable findings were repaired in one finalization pass and none was declined.

The largest was a coverage gap, not a slip. The syllabus outcome behind this graph node, BIO-124, requires comparing receptor classes and tracing a signal through to cross-talk. The candidate traced one canonical Wnt example, and its own attribution file declared a receptor-class survey out of scope. Two scenes now close that: a comparison reading four receptor architectures as predictions about what crosses the membrane and how the signal stops, and a scene on reading more than one input at once, which is placed directly after the scene bounding what a single gradient can specify because it is the answer to that limit. Six new sources support them, all from PMC.

Two corrections went to the heart of the lesson's quantitative argument.

  • The direction of the noise term was wrong. The worked example said that loosening its assumptions, including the noiseless one, raises the information supply. The theoretical work cited says noise entropy can only subtract. Independence and graded reading raise the figure; noise lowers it, which makes the number an optimistic ceiling rather than a floor. The two kinds of assumption are now kept apart in the scene and in the practice task that repeated the error.
  • A binary threshold carries at most one bit, and a full bit only when its two outcomes are equally likely. The count of thresholds is an upper bound on the bits they supply, before noise.

Two answer keys required an account the pack itself does not hold.

  • The ordering item made recruitment of the destruction complex to the membrane a mandatory causal stage, while the pack's own claim records that mechanism as unsettled, with saturation and impaired ubiquitin-ligase docking also proposed. The item now asks for the observed sequence and instructs the marker not to penalise a learner who adds that the causal link is open.
  • The APC item keyed complete Wnt independence as a categorical consequence of truncation. The study cited reports retained localisation and partial regulation, and the pack's own claim says the degree of decoupling depends on which part of APC is lost. The stem now fixes which regions are lost, and the final part asks the learner to name a feature of the truncation that would change the answer.

The amplification audit was also drawing more from its numbers than they carry. A sixfold ratio of two steady states is not a gain without the input change and the operating range; one-to-one receptor occupancy does not establish that nothing multiplies downstream over time; and high gain does not by itself entail early saturation, which depends on dose-response shape, dynamic range, feedback, adaptation and input scale. Each is now stated at the strength the evidence supports.

Two minor corrections: the practice scene restates four claims it was not mapped to, and repetition in practice does not exempt a claim from carrying its evidence; and "cascade" is a convention that a textbook records as common usage rather than an exclusive definition, so the pack now says it is holding to the narrower sense and why.

Recorded rather than resolved: no timescale is asserted for any receptor class, because the only sourced figures are ionotropic against metabotropic in chemoreception and say nothing about receptor tyrosine kinases or nuclear receptors. The table has no speed column, the scene says why, and an assessment distractor offers exactly that inference so a learner is asked to refuse it.
